sampling_model.design: Independent replicate wells are collected at fixed, known integer composition rows of \(M\), with exact raw-count addition and no unknown thinning or normalization. The two-row matrix \(M_0\) and both prescribed three-node inputs are synthetic prospective designs whose certification status remains open.
sampling_model.units: A unit is one replicate well containing exactly the declared number of independent cells of each labeled type; rowwise random splitting produces \(N_A\) training wells and \(N_B\) inference wells, both split sizes diverge, and the row fractions converge to a normalized rational probability vector \(\rho\) that is strictly positive for every sampled composition row.
sampling_model.treatment: For \(p\geq3\), the ordered embedding \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\) is fixed before analysis. Broad published-class membership is used only for labeled-DAG recovery. The interventions \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=1)\) and \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=2)\), and responses \(V_{i_Y}\) and \(V_{i_Z}\), are evaluated by truncated factorization only in the causally sufficient compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass.
sampling_model.overlap: Positive Poisson roots and rates give full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\) in the strict benchmark subclass, so every parent configuration used in its truncated-factorization functional has positive observational probability. No such Poisson-root or full-support claim is imposed on the broader published CPCM class used only for graph recovery.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pooled PGFs are empirical replicate-well averages; component PGFs use the full-rank log inverse; graph and parameter estimates use the deterministic lexicographic sample-split selector. The certifier always returns one of three statuses, but inference is activated only by \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\), after normalized positive row allocation, wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local nonsingularity, positive interiority clearance, tail control, and precision have all been verified.

Theorems 1--2 identify component distributions up to shifts, and Section 4 estimates transform mixtures by GMM.
Theorem 2 obtains component recovery under pairwise column independence for a generalized-hyperexponential approximation class.
Definitions 9--10 define the causally minimal and pairwise-identifiable CPCM setting, allowing arbitrary source-node laws, and Lemma 11 identifies its DAG from the direct joint law.

Definition 3 specifies PT-SEM from direct observational count vectors; Theorem 12 identifies its DAG, thinning matrix, and node-wise exogenous distributions under (A1)--(A3), and Theorem 18 proves plug-in BIC selection consistency under (A1)--(A5).
Section 4.2 studies functional consistency under linear aggregation and gives affine ANM/PNL consequences; Section 4.3 concerns conditional-independence consistency.
The paper establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and covariance weighting for finite or continuum moments.
The article develops mathematically rigorous verification methods based on directed floating-point and interval arithmetic.
The article distinguishes rigorous from non-rigorous deterministic branch-and-bound and reviews sound interval relaxations and termination claims.
The paper combines Taylor-model enclosures with branch-and-bound for rigorous global search.
The paper constructs rigorous interval quasiconvex relaxations for self-validating constrained global optimization.
Theorems 2 and 4 certify approximate polynomial roots and common associated roots.
The paper optimizes network-tomography probe allocation using Fisher information.

body.tldr: Known linearly independent raw-count compositions recover unrestricted labeled type laws for arbitrary \(p\geq1\) by a logarithmic count-PGF inverse, with positive Poisson aliases proving necessity. Any recovered count-valued law in the published pairwise-identifiable CPCM class then has its labeled DAG identified; intervention contrasts and validation use the stricter compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass. For \(p\geq3\), the headline is a finite sound tri-valued certifier: it always terminates, and only a \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output verifies a rational chart-projection cover together with wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local Jacobian nonsingularity, interiority, PGF-tail, and designated-contrast precision bounds. The finite-grid theorem separately proves existence of some finite rational grid and cover with positive exact margins; it does not certify either prescribed synthetic input. Pointwise sample-split Wald inference is conditional on certification, the capped certified-design frontier is finite, and the three-node base/conditional-refinement benchmark status remains open.

project_justification.gap: Transform inversion, Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin's direct-law CPCM theorem, and validated-numerics methods are established separately. The published CPCM result starts from a direct count-valued joint law and does not recover labeled type laws through known multi-composition pools; existing validated-numerics results do not jointly propagate infinite-support PGF tails through graph exclusion, remote within-graph separation, local chart injectivity, Jacobian regularity, covariance, and intervention precision.
project_justification.niche: Prospective known-composition designs need a proof-producing bridge from aggregate raw-count laws to labeled cellular laws and then to the broadest justified graph class, with intervention and inference claims explicitly confined to a compact certifiable polynomial subclass.
project_justification.fill: The project composes the arbitrary-dimensional rank frontier with published pairwise-identifiable CPCM DAG recovery, proves causal minimality of the strict positive-polynomial benchmark directly from its positive edge coefficients, and supplies for \(p\geq3\) an always-terminating one-sided-sound certifier plus a finite capped design frontier. Relative eventual certification is proved only under explicit strict exact slack and uniform convergence of all numerical controls; no prescribed synthetic input is claimed to meet those premises.

body.related_work: Shih--Hero is credited for logarithmic transform inversion of independent additive components; the integer-multiplicity multivariate count-PGF recovery map and positive unrestricted converse are derived here. Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin Definitions 9--10 describe the causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM setting, and their direct-law DAG result is composed with labeled unpooling here. The positive-polynomial Poisson subclass is shown, edge by edge, to be causally minimal and pairwise identifiable rather than acquiring those properties by definition. Carrasco--Florens and Newey--McFadden supply finite-moment minimum-distance ingredients. Rump, Kearfott, and Berz--Makino motivate validated arithmetic, interval global search, and Taylor enclosures. The new validation step jointly carries analytic Poisson-PGF tails through wrong-graph exclusion, the corrected one-sided remote-subset branch, rational chart covers, Jacobian and covariance checks, and designated causal precision. Its relative eventual-certification theorem is conditional on strict exact slack and convergent controls, not an assertion about the two fixed synthetic runs.
body.interpretation: Full column rank first identifies each labeled cellular observational law; it does not define a graph or an intervention. The recovered law identifies a labeled DAG on the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class. Intervention contrasts require the narrower causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass, whose full support identifies the kernels in the truncated factorization. The certificate handle enumerates the declared finite design class, records all three statuses, and promotes only \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) inputs to the Pareto comparison. Fixed controls always terminate but can remain undecided. Along a control sequence, eventual certification follows only from the separately stated strict-slack and uniform-convergence hypotheses.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The leaf ceiling and outward-rounded operation bound are unconditional finite ceilings, not efficiency guarantees. The \(27\)-point floating-point pilot and its two pointwise Jacobian singular values certify neither compact-box graph separation nor remote identification, chart coverage, tails, covariance, or useful contrast precision. Compactness converts strict exact slack into eventual positivity of sufficiently accurate lower enclosures, and the corrected remote rule permits a boundary-straddling box to pass from positive moment distance alone. That result is relative: without the stipulated strict margins and convergent truncation, Taylor, subdivision, and rounding controls, the procedure may return \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\). Neither fixed synthetic input currently has a validated proof object.
body.honest_scope: Unrestricted rank recovery and stability apply for arbitrary \(p\geq1\). Labeled-DAG transfer applies to recovered laws in the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable count-valued CPCM class and imposes no Poisson source law. Intervention contrasts, finite-grid construction, certification, and Wald inference are confined to the compact causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass and, for the designated contrasts, require \(p\geq3\) and fixed \(\iota\). Certification is always terminating and one-sided sound but may be undecided. Eventual certification is conditional on strict positive exact graph, remote, chart, Jacobian, interiority, algebraic, and precision margins together with uniform numerical convergence; it certifies neither prescribed benchmark by itself. Covariance and Wald claims additionally require normalized strictly positive row fractions and give pointwise, not uniform post-selection, coverage. No claim covers unknown thinning, normalization, composition error, shared-well dependence, hidden types, high-dimensional growth, or biologically calibrated coefficient boxes.
